newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo sees synergies in internal restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Volvo sees synergies in internal restructuring.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Thursday it expected significant synergy effects from stepping up cooperation with various divisions within the company.

Speaking at a Volvo seminar, Volvo managing director Leif Johansson said that when Volvo planned the merger with Renault, which failed in 1993, the Swedish company split up into various companies and there were synergies from bringing them together.

"In connection with the Renault deal the company was split up and I believe there are now significant synergies to be gained from increased cooperations between the various (Volvo) companies," he said.
Johansson named areas such as purchasing, development of new internal combustion engines and establishing units on new markets.
In the short term, cost synergies will be most significant but in the long term income synergies will be most important, Johansson said.
"The Volvo group will grow and I think this means more synergies to utilise," he said.
Johansson said increased European integration would enable Volvo to concentrate the different companies' operations at strategic locations.

"The increased integration in Europe makes it easier for us to merge import and marketing companies for the different units to centres in Europe," Johansson said. "Another example is the distribution of spare parts."
Johansson referred to Swedish ball bearing company SKF's concentration of European operations as a successful example.
Possible synergies vary in the different units but no Volvo unit is about to be sold, Johansson said.
